pillars.title: Making nonlinear ideas constructive
pillars.text: Geometry and analysis become practical feedback designs, with passivity and Lyapunov methods connecting stability, robustness and optimality.

pillars.title: Geometry as a language for algorithms
pillars.text: Respecting the shape of a search space leads to useful numerical methods, and links mathematical structure with computation.

pillars.title: Coordination without a conductor
pillars.text: Relative information and coupling organize collective motion. Synchronization, balancing and geometric consensus supply a precise intellectual basis for the musical idea of an ensemble.

pillars.title: Finding simple structure in complex dynamics
pillars.text: Differential methods extend tools familiar from linear control to nonlinear systems. Dominance makes low-dimensional long-term behaviour accessible to an interconnection theory.

pillars.title: Sensitivity and robustness across scales
pillars.text: Positive and negative feedback work together. Cellular regulation shapes circuit behaviour, while switching and tuning can remain distinct design functions.

pillars.title: Rhythm as an open system
pillars.text: Repeated events become useful through adaptation to the environment. Spiking links continuous physical dynamics with reliable event timing, extending feedback questions into new forms of computation and control.
